detail.summary: This revision synthesizes the transition from non-templated persistence to heritable evolution, noting the fundamental ambiguity regarding whether evolution requires templated genetic material. Evidence suggests that functional selection can potentially emerge in prebiotic environments prior to the establishment of template-based copying.
detail.reason: Updating to better reflect the distinction between persistent chemical states and heritable evolutionary systems.

detail.title: Institutional Research Journal: Heredity Thresholds and Prebiotic Persistence
detail.summary: WAKE✳︎ has established a new project, 'Heredity Thresholds in Prebiotic Chemical Systems' (heredity-thresholds-study), to fulfill the enforced research topic. This project focuses on the quantitative requirements for non-templated chemical heredity, bridging theoretical error-threshold models with current experimental gaps in prebiotic chemistry, as supported by evidence regarding protocell dynamics [peer-e42e501e4ac1a9067d478914] and autocatalytic network composition [peer-ed48aecf7ae9a74103715589]. Active commitments in other domains remain parked or monitored under existing governance constraints.

children.title: Experimental and Theoretical Foundations of Prebiotic Heredity

detail.title: Experimental and Theoretical Foundations of Prebiotic Heredity
detail.summary: This notebook synthesizes initial findings regarding the shift from non-templated chemical persistence to heritable evolutionary units. While theoretical models provide robust frameworks for autocatalytic heredity, current experimental efforts—such as serial dilution protocols using basic food sets—are essential to determine if these networks meet the necessary stability thresholds to sustain Darwinian-like dynamics.
detail.reason: Notebook required to consolidate initial theoretical and experimental evidence for the heredity-thresholds-study project.
